status.evidence: According to the UK Companies House registry, Quartix Limited is currently active and is owned by Quartix Technologies plc.

claims.claim: The company reports that its core tracking devices (TCSV11 and TCSV12) utilize firmware embedded in an ST Micro 32-bit ARM M3 Cortex microcontroller that supports 100ms GPS sampling (1Hz event monitoring) and relays data over 2G/4G cellular networks via 30-second updates, as detailed on the Quartix Technology Page.
claims.corrected: The company reports that its core tracking devices (TCSV11 and TCSV12) utilize firmware embedded in an ST Micro 32-bit ARM M3 Cortex microcontroller that supports 100ms GPS sampling (10Hz event monitoring) and relays data over 2G/4G cellular networks via 30-second updates, as detailed on the Quartix Technology Page.

claims.claim: The company reports that its client WJ Road Markings integrated Quartix telematics data via an API into the FuelTek fuel management system to automate odometer readings, achieving a 12% improvement in MPG and £160,000 in maintenance and operational savings, according to a case study on the Quartix website.
claims.source: Quartix WJ Road Markings Case Study

claims.claim: The company reports its TCSV12 OBD plug-in and TCSV11 hardwired tracking hardware support a 10Hz GPS receiver, a 100/800Hz tri-axis accelerometer, a 32-bit ARM Cortex M3 MCU, and an operating temperature range of -30°C to +80°C, according to the official Quartix Limited technical specification document.

The company reports that its hardwired trackers connect directly to 12V or 24V electrical systems, support tamper detection alerts, and can integrate with specialized external vehicle sensors and inputs, including Driver ID key fobs, emergency doors, and tailgate lifts, according to the official Quartix Limited fleet deployment specifications.

The company reports processing all telematics data within ISO 27001-certified data centres in the United Kingdom and maintains certification under the UK Government Cyber Essentials scheme for information technology security.

The company reports providing secure API data access within its Enterprise plan tier to extract vehicle tracking details and develop custom internal system integrations, as detailed on the Quartix Integrations and Partnerships Platform.

The company reports serving over 35,000 global fleet customers and having installed more than 1 million GPS tracking units since 2001, including a specific active deployment by WJ Road Markings where driver behaviour reports helped optimize 420 fleet vehicles, as outlined on the Quartix UK website.

Quartix was awarded a place as an active supplier on the Crown Commercial Service (CCS) RM6315 Vehicle Telematics Solutions Framework agreement in May 2024, facilitating compliance-regulated telematics deployment for UK public sector bodies and local authorities.

The company reports in its 2025 financial statements that its total group revenue increased by 12% to £35.7 million compared to £31.8 million in 2024, while its profit before tax rose by 34% to £8.7 million, as published in its 2025 Annual Report.

The company reports in its H1 2026 interim results presentation that the UK remains its largest absolute operational region, maintaining approximately £20 million in annualized recurring revenue, with its connected dashcam solution serving as a significant contributor to UK growth throughout 2025.

Quartix Limited announced a strategic partnership with Autoglass®, a prominent UK vehicle glass repair and replacement specialist, to offer exclusive service discounts to fleet operator clients right from the start of their telematics subscription.

The company operates a formalized Reseller and Sales Partner Program targeting B2B service providers across the automotive, insurance, telecoms, and leasing sectors, reporting an active network of over 230 global business partners.

The company reports that its global fleet subscription base reached 333,922 units and its total customer base grew to 32,942 at the end of December 2025, with UK operations generating £18.0 million out of £35.7 million in total group revenue, according to the Quartix Technologies plc Annual Report 2025.

The company reports that its UK offices handle technical support, onboarding, and customer service inquiries during fixed business hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Friday, supplemented by a contracted installation network of more than 250 engineers across the UK, as detailed in the official Quartix Onboarding and Contact Guides.
claims.source: Quartix Support Knowledge Base (https://site.com) and Onboarding Guide (https://www.quartix.com/en-gb/onboarding/)
